$comment: Single source of truth for Orion's visual design. Edit HERE, then run build-tokens.py to regenerate the CSS block in the mockup and the Swift constants in the app. Never hand-edit the generated output.

color.$comment: Neutrals are deliberately near-perfectly neutral. A gray biased toward the accent reads as 'considered' in most interfaces; in a raw editor it reads as a color cast and corrupts the judgment the app exists to support.

groove.use: A slider's engraved channel. Darker than ground so a horizontal track stands off the panel it lies on; ground alone was seven levels from the panel and the track vanished (2026-10-28)

hover.use: A hovered or pressed control's fill

surround.use: Canvas surround — what the photo is judged against

rail.use: Scrollbar thumbs, and the lit lower lip of a slider's groove (AnalogTrack); tinted tracks draw their own label gradient (TrackTint)

label.use: A control's name (slider and field labels): a step above dim notes

faint.use: Inactive icons, detents, separators. Not for words a person must read: 2.5:1 on panel, under AA (dim is 5.0:1)

accent.use: Interactive and active states ONLY. Never decorative.

warn.use: What a person must see: a failed render or write, clipped highlights, an unreadable file. Star's value today, its own role so either can move

filmBase.use: Film base — the darkest value in the interface, under the strip

filmHole.use: Sprocket perforations and the rebate edge — a hole shows the light through

space.$comment: The scale, and nothing between: 2 · 4 · 6 · 10 · 14 · 18 · 26. Tight inside a group (xs, gap, sm), generous between groups (pad, lg, xl). Panel padding is 14 rather than 16 — pro tool panels want density. Not spacing, so not here: 1 px hairlines, a ring's offset from what it rings, the macOS traffic lights' 80 px.

radius.$comment: sm for chips, swatches and keycaps; md for controls and cells; lg for a well that holds md controls 2 px in, so the corners stay concentric (md + 2). A pill is half its height and needs no token.

type.$comment: The scale: 11 · 12 · 13 for the working text (a 1 px step, dense tool), then about 1.3× per step for the few large words: 17 a sheet's title, 28 the empty canvas's wordmark. xs (10) stays only for the old mockup; no numeral is under 11. System face for words. On macOS this IS SF Pro, so the mockup renders exactly what SwiftUI will. Numbers are the exception: `numeral`, set at weight 500 with tabular figures (DESIGN.md), bundled under SIL OFL 1.1.

shadow.$comment: One shadow: the lift under what a hand grabs (a slider thumb, the wheel's puck, the compare handle). Black at alpha, offset down, soft. Hover and press move offset and blur from here (AnalogTrack).

icon.$comment: Every glyph is drawn on a 24-unit grid and keeps it: a box of `sm` or `md` points shows the grid scaled, never stretched to the glyph's own bounds, so an X and a sun at one size read as one set (Shared/Icons.cs). Two sizes: `sm` for a mark inside a row of text (a chevron, a kind, a caption's stars), `md` for a glyph on a button, a tab or a section's nameplate (a full-grid glyph draws about 13 there). One stroke, `stroke` points at every size.
